recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is for core reconciliation. If current generated Java artifacts still mishandle percent-containing codes, open a focused follow-up against the current generator owner, likely HL7/kindling, using fd705833 as the historical implementation reference.
issue_request: FHIR-12427 was a Published/Persuasive DSTU2 FHIR-core change request asking the Java code generator to replace '%' with 'pct' when deriving Java enum or constant names from binding code values such as observation-statistics '%20' and '%80'.
initial_application: Historical commit fd70583337b3caf1e62b58e43978f5535c33a724, tagged #12427 and svn build@10496, added '%' special handling and cc.replace("%", "pct") to JavaBaseGenerator.makeConst, matching the Jira resolution.
additional_context: The current FHIR specification checkout has no Java generator source and no JavaBaseGenerator/makeConst implementation. Later history removed the old reference implementation/generator tree, while the current Gradle build depends on org.hl7.fhir:kindling and invokes org.hl7.fhir.tools.publisher.Publisher from that classpath. The current observation-statistics source also now uses 20-percent and 80-percent rather than the original leading-percent codes.
reconciliation: Published an empty external-repo audit commit on the combined branch. Any remaining generator behavior belongs in the current external generator/tooling repository rather than in the HL7/fhir source checkout.
